title: Olaudah Equiano
summary: Olaudah Equiano, also called Gustavus Vassa, was a formerly enslaved sailor and writer who became a leading voice against the slave trade in Britain. His 1789 Interesting Narrative describes birth in Igboland; baptismal and naval records instead name South Carolina, and the question is unresolved.

uncertainty.note: Birth is given as c. 1745 on the opened page; the birthplace itself is disputed. Death is dated only to March 1797 on the opened page.

where.modern_name: Anambra State, Nigeria (Igbo area; his own account names "Eboe"/Essaka, near the River Niger). Alternative account: South Carolina.
where.historical_name: "Eboe" in Guinea, in his own account (Interesting Narrative); the 1759 baptismal record and a 1773 naval muster instead give South Carolina

importance.justification: Author of one of the most widely read 18th-century slave narratives and a prominent abolitionist campaigner in Britain.

sources.title: Author casts shadow over slave hero
sources.publisher: University of Texas at Austin, Africa Online Digest archive

sources.title: Wikidata item Q117714 (Anambra State), coordinate location (P625)

reviewer_note: Birthplace is contested: the pin is the centre of Anambra State, Nigeria, as a coarse stand-in for his own account of an Igbo birth; Carretta's South Carolina evidence (1759 baptismal record, 1773 muster) is recorded in the summary, not pinned. Birth year c. 1745 rests on one opened page; the exact death day was not confirmed on an opened page.
